cases.detail: Verilator 5.052 evaluates the index of an indexed part-select target of an assignment operator twice: v[next_bit() +: 2] += 2'd1 calls next_bit() once for the read and again for the write, so the sum lands in other bits. IEEE 1800-2023 11.4.1 evaluates a left-hand index expression of an assignment operator only once; Verilator does so for a bit-select target, and the standalone source reproduces the difference. xezim 0.11.3 calls it once.

cases.detail: Verilator 5.052 writes bits that IEEE 1800-2023 11.5.1 discards: the out-of-range bit of a partially out-of-range indexed part-select (minus_write[i -: 2] with i = 0) lands in bit 7, a constant part-select wholly outside the vector (comb_out[11:8]) writes its low bits, a partly outside one of an ascending vector (comb_up[6:9]) takes the wrong end of the value, and run-time selects within one array element whose positions are known at compile time reach past it. Icarus agrees with the expected values.
